# Shibuya building photo references

Research checked 2026-10-07 UTC. These are visual references for original low-poly geometry; do not copy photos into the game or use them as textures. A permissive photo license applies to the photo only, not necessarily to trademarks, building design, tenant signage, or other depicted rights. For proprietary property listings and articles, use the linked page as view-only reference. The reference photos are not dimensioned drawings; do not infer or publish precise dimensions from perspective photos.

## Best shared guidance

- For a light, original Dogenzaka street asset, use a simple 5–6-storey narrow commercial box with a recessed street entry, one open external stair/landing stack, small shop windows, a restrained stack of fictional tenant boards, and a plain parapet. The observed Odawaraya example has six storeys and a zigzag external stair; do not reproduce its exact sign layout, tenant names, or facade pattern.
- A restaurant frontage can reuse the same simple massing but emphasize a door/window at sidewalk level, a short awning or noren, one projecting lantern/sign, a menu board, and visible pipes/cables. Nonbei Yokocho is a good Shibuya-scale reference for those street cues, though its photo is a lane of tiny storefronts rather than one complete building.
- For a residential archetype, use stacked recessed balconies, narrow rails/dividers, a mostly quiet facade, a modest entry court/drive, and small street greenery. Sakuragaoka’s Park Axis towers are 14 storeys; if the game brief calls for a lower mid-rise, make that a clearly original synthesis rather than claiming it is Park Axis.
- Prefer modular floors and a small set of materials/sign planes. Keep brand names, logos, exact facade geometry, and photo textures out of the asset. Source photos with CC0 or CC BY-SA do not need to be included in the game's asset package for visual research.

## QFRONT / crossing retail

### Commons photos

1. **Qfront.jpg** — [file page](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Qfront.jpg). Photographer/uploader ITA-ATU, own photo, 2008-05-05; 480 × 640. Commons says it is the Shibuya landmark Q-FRONT and the uploader released this photo to the public domain (`PD-self`). Location confidence: named landmark and Shibuya on the Commons description/category; no camera coordinates listed. Reuse of the photo itself is marked public domain with no conditions, but do not use it as a texture or treat that as permission to copy the real building or marks. Accessed 2026-10-07.

2. **QFront-Shibuya-01.jpg** — [file page](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:QFront-Shibuya-01.jpg). Photographer/uploader Rs1421, own photo, September 2011; 900 × 1,200. Description identifies QFRONT at Jinnan 1-chome, Shibuya; category QFRONT. License `CC BY-SA 3.0`: credit author, link the license, note changes; adaptations must use the same or a compatible license. Accessed 2026-10-07.

3. **Shibuya Q-Front at night.jpg** — [file page](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Shibuya_Q-Front_at_night.jpg). Patrick Dep / Flickr, taken 2008-12-22; 1,280 × 960. The Commons file description and categories place it at Shibuya Crossing / Q-Front; camera point 35.659004, 139.702234. License `CC BY-SA 2.0`: credit, license link, change notice, share-alike for adaptations. This is useful for night-lighting and street-corner context. Accessed 2026-10-07.

### Building facts

- [Tokyu REIT QFRONT profile](https://www.tokyu-reit.co.jp/portfolio/detail?id=1) gives address 21-6 Udagawacho, 8 floors above ground plus 3 basement levels, October 1999 completion, 784.26 m² site area, and 6,675.52 m² total floor area. Accessed 2026-10-07. Those are reported source facts, not a dimensioned facade plan. If a game envelope is inferred from the parcel/floor-area figures, keep it explicitly labeled as a game-scale estimate.
- Image-search previews show a rounded/glazed street-facing corner, large digital sign area, and retail frontage. The crossing-retail author is directly inspecting the Commons photos for geometry; prefer that first-hand visual check for any exact silhouette detail.

## Shibuya PARCO / terraced retail

1. **Shibuya PARCO 2.jpg** — [file page](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Shibuya_PARCO_2.jpg). Photographer/uploader Syced, own photo, 2023-09-02; 4,080 × 3,072; camera point 35.661775, 139.698689. Commons identifies Shibuya PARCO and the point is in the PARCO/Udagawacho area. License `CC0 1.0`; the photographer waives copyright rights to the photo to the extent allowed, including commercial reuse without permission. Attribution is appreciated. Accessed 2026-10-07.

2. **Shibuya Parco 191229c.jpg** — [file page](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Shibuya_Parco_191229c.jpg). Photographer/uploader 江戸村のとくぞう, own photo, 2019-12-29; 3,000 × 4,496. The photo is a current-building-era reference. Check the file page’s stated license before any reuse; use as visual study only here. Accessed 2026-10-07.

3. **Shibuya PARCO.jpg** — [file page](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Shibuya_PARCO.jpg). ITA-ATU, own photo, 2008-05-05; 480 × 640; marked `PD-self`. This is the earlier pre-rebuild PARCO, not the 2019 building, and should not be used to model the current terraced form.

Visual cues from image previews and the terraced-retail author's direct review of article photos: contemporary PARCO reads as stacked white volumes with deep terrace recesses/overhangs, glass retail at grade, planting at upper terraces, and a finer vertical-mullion tower element. The author reviewed [Tatefro's article/photos](https://tatefro.com/entry-93.html) (outside_2, outside_4, spiral-walk_3, spiral-walk_5), accessed 2026-10-07. Its photo reuse license is not established here, so use that source only to study form. Avoid copying the building's exact logo or branded retail signs.

## Dogenzaka narrow mixed-use buildings and restaurant street

### Exact Dogenzaka location / block context

1. **Odawaraya Building exterior** — [property listing](https://www.oasis-estate.jp/building/36007); [photo](https://www.oasis-estate.jp/img/uploads/properties/36007/ZyyJqVhUzM1638174558.jpg). The listing identifies Odawaraya Building at 2-25-10 Dogenzaka, completed September 1981, six storeys, RC construction. The direct photo was visually inspected by the Dogenzaka model author. Visible cues: very narrow building between larger neighbors; pale cream/brown facade; zigzag exterior stair/landing stack; repeated business signs; recessed street-level entry below a wide fascia. No open photo license was found on the listing, so it is copyrighted/view-only: no photo or texture reuse. Accessed 2026-10-07.

2. **Nishinaya No.2** — [property listing](https://offisite.jp/office/9921); [photo](https://offisite.jp/media/filter/lg-wm/buildings/3/5/35e1b1f725d26fb4703c34a127a8c61f-340rvsu97y6848a7.jpg). Search-image preview describes a narrow brown four-storey building between taller neighbors, with large windows/metal panels and a ground-floor cafe/tenant frontage. No reuse license confirmed; view-only. Accessed 2026-10-07.

3. **Obayashi Building** — [property listing](https://www.oasis-estate.jp/building/35583); [photo](https://www.oasis-estate.jp/img/uploads/properties/35583/8vJO3oimT41656586659.jpg). Listed at 2-25-7 Dogenzaka, 5 floors above ground plus 1 basement, completed April 1986. Search-image preview shows a narrow light-panel facade, small cylindrical balconies, and a street-level bar sign. No reuse license confirmed; view-only. Accessed 2026-10-07.

4. **Dogenzaka shibuya 2403.jpg** — [Commons file page](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Dogenzaka_shibuya_2403.jpg). Photographer/uploader 鋸香具師, own photo, 2024-03-06; 2,000 × 1,500. Japanese description says it is the middle of Dogenzaka, looking toward Shibuya Station; Commons category Dōgenzaka. License `CC0 1.0`, photo may be reused commercially without permission; credit appreciated. No camera GPS in the file metadata. Accessed 2026-10-07.

5. **Dogenzaka 2-26 new buildings / dogenzaka-dori** — [Commons file page](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Dogenzaka_2-26_new_buildings,_dogenzaka-dori_道玄坂通.jpg). Syced, own photo, 2023-08-05; 3,072 × 4,080; camera point 35.660383, 139.697481. Commons tags Bunkamura Street and Dōgenzaka. `CC0 1.0`. Useful for contemporary redevelopment frontage/context, but it is new/high-rise development rather than the narrow mid-block archetype. Accessed 2026-10-07.

### Street-level restaurant cues

1. **Shibuya-Nonbe-Yokocho-02.jpg** — [Commons file page](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Shibuya-Nonbe-Yokocho-02.jpg); [original photo](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/69/Shibuya-Nonbe-Yokocho-02.jpg). Photographer/uploader Rs1421, own photo, May 2011; 1,200 × 900. Commons identifies Nonbei Yokocho, Shibuya, Tokyo and category Nonbei Yokochō; no camera coordinates listed. License `CC BY-SA 3.0`: credit and license link, note changes, share-alike for adaptations. Directly inspected: very narrow lane, tiny ground-level restaurant doors, dark/wood storefronts and noren, dense vertical Japanese signs, red-white paper lanterns overhead, exposed utilities/pipes and some greenery. Good for street texture and human scale; not a full standalone building image. Accessed 2026-10-07.

2. **Shibuya Night Scene (11920317934).jpg** — [Commons file page](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Shibuya_Night_Scene_(11920317934).jpg). Stephen Kelly via Flickr, taken 2013-09-09; 3,264 × 4,928. Commons categories identify Hakata Fūryū, restaurants in Shibuya, Hyakken-dana and Dōgenzaka; no camera coordinates listed. `CC BY 2.0`: credit, link the license, note changes. Useful Shibuya Dogenzaka/Hakendana restaurant-night context; avoid copying signs/branding. Accessed 2026-10-07.

3. **Outback steakhouse Shibuya.jpg** — [Commons file page](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Outback_steakhouse_Shibuya.jpg); [original photo](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/b6/Outback_steakhouse_Shibuya.jpg). Wideangle, own work, 2010-08-06; 3,264 × 2,448; Commons places it in Restaurants in Shibuya ward. The image was directly inspected by a research worker: street-facing multi-tenant block, exposed stair to an upper restaurant, neighboring Japanese shop signs and planters. `CC BY-SA 3.0` is listed (page also presents GFDL/older CC BY-SA choices); follow the selected license's attribution, license-link, change notice and share-alike terms. Brand-specific/outdated; use for physical frontage/stair study only. Accessed 2026-10-07.

## Sakuragaoka residential / office mid-rise

1. **Construction seen from Shibuya Stream 2.jpg** — [Commons file page](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Construction_seen_from_Shibuya_Stream_2.jpg). Photographer/uploader Syced; uploaded 2023-01-13; 2,924 × 4,986; viewpoint/object location 35.655455, 139.702966. Commons description says the elevated view looks south-southwest over Sakuragaoka-cho and specifically identifies two white towers as Park Axis Shibuya Sakuragaoka South (left rear) and West (right), each 14 floors and completed in 2006. License `CC0 1.0`; commercial reuse of the photo is permitted without permission, credit appreciated. Strong specific location/identity source; it is a pair of 14-storey towers, not a 7-storey mid-rise. Accessed 2026-10-07.

2. **Park Axis Shibuya Sakuragaoka West** — [Ken Corporation listing](https://www.kencorp.com/rent/yokohamaapartment/search/results/151467.html); [listing image](https://www.kencorp.com/assets/image/building/151467/151467_q1.jpg). A Sakuragaoka model author directly inspected this image. Visible cues: stacked balconies at every floor, alternating dark/light horizontal facade bands, landscaped street-level entrance/drive and overhead power lines. Listing identifies this as a 14-storey RC building completed September 2006. This is a proprietary real-estate image with no open reuse grant stated; view-only, no texture reuse. Accessed 2026-10-07.

3. **Sakuragaoka Urban Life B** — [Tokyu Livable property page](https://www.livable.co.jp/mansion/library/000000015909/); [listing photo](https://www.livable.co.jp/project-image/15/159/15909/15909_22553380.jpg?20180410182655). The Sakuragaoka model author directly inspected it as a second residential precedent. Property listing images are copyrighted/view-only unless separately licensed. Accessed 2026-10-07.

4. **15 Sakuragaoka-cho, Shibuya.jpg** — [Commons file page](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:15_Sakuragaoka-cho,_Shibuya.jpg). Momotarou2012, own photo dated 2012-12-09; 2,800 × 2,100. Commons says around 15 Sakuragaoka-cho and categorizes it as a curved building, streetcorner shop, Sukiya restaurant, and slope. `CC BY-SA 3.0`: credit, license link, change notice, share-alike for adaptations. This is a local streetscape detail reference, not evidence of a residential building. Accessed 2026-10-07.

5. **Shibuya Sanshin Mansion** — [Office Navi listing](https://en.office-navi.jp/building/02023338/); the image result is on the listing. Search-image preview identifies a 7-storey RC building at 29-33 Sakuragaokacho, with three tiers of glass-panel balconies, dark accents, a low perimeter wall, and sloping street. Listing imagery is proprietary/view-only; useful if a 7-storey visual precedent is needed, but verify on the source page and do not reuse the photograph. Accessed 2026-10-07.

## Additional Shibuya analogs retained from the broader search

1. **Tanta building shibuya.jpg** — [Commons file page](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Tanta_building_shibuya.jpg); [original photo](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/1/1a/Tanta_building_shibuya.jpg?utm_source=commons.wikimedia.org&utm_campaign=index&utm_content=original). Photographer/uploader 鋸香具師, own work, taken 2023-10-31. Commons Japanese description identifies Studio Tanta at 1-11-1 Tomigaya, Shibuya, as recording studios and restaurants, at the northwest corner of Yoyogi Park Police Box intersection (35.668009, 139.691494). The actual image was visually inspected by a research worker: compact rounded-corner mid-rise, repetitive concrete framing/glazed bands, glassy ground floor and mixed-use frontage. `CC0 1.0`; commercial reuse of the photo is permitted without permission, credit appreciated. This is a useful type analogy but Tomigaya, not Dogenzaka. Accessed 2026-10-07.

2. **Narrow building with rounded balconies in Shibuya.jpg** — [Commons file page](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Narrow_building_with_rounded_balconies_in_Shibuya.jpg); [original photo](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/61/Narrow_building_with_rounded_balconies_in_Shibuya.jpg). Grendelkhan, own photo, 2018-04-19; 1,768 × 4,618; camera point 35.667781, 139.690967; categorized by Commons as a Shibuya residential building. The actual image was visually inspected by a research worker: very slender massing, stacked rounded balconies with deep soffits/glazed rails, neighboring-building gap, and entry stair. `CC BY-SA 4.0`: credit, license link, change notice; adaptations under same/compatible license. Useful as silhouette only; it does not evidence commercial use. Accessed 2026-10-07.

## Research limits

- Several source pages may change, and some Wikimedia image hosts were not retrievable in this environment. The Commons file pages remain the canonical place to confirm current authorship, source, date, dimensions, and license before use.
- Visual observations explicitly marked as direct inspection came from the building authors/research worker using the source images. For remaining references, use the file/page metadata and confirm geometry with a pixel-level inspection before making fine-grained claims.
- `CC0`, `PD-self`, and `CC BY-SA` status covers the identified image. Do not assume it grants a right to reuse the original photographed building's logo, trade dress, advertising, or proprietary architectural design. No real photographs should be shipped as game textures in this task.
